source.title: Self-Distillation Bridges Distribution Gap in Language Model Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Zhaorui Yang; Qian Liu; Tianyu Pang; Han Wang; H. Feng; Min-Feng Zhu; Wei Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign task fine-tuning changes harmful-request safety, and whether appended adversarial suffixes affect safety, using safe-response rates rather than the original study's method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports safety results for vanilla fine-tuning and SDFT on benign task datasets, with and without appended adversarial suffixes. Cited findings from other studies are not rows. Non-safety benchmarks and the paper's distribution-shift metrics do not measure the claim versions. The safety measure is keyword matching on AdvBench; the suffix evaluation uses fixed adversarial suffixes.
record.test_reason: Vanilla LoRA and full fine-tuning of Llama-2-chat (7B, 13B) and Llama-3-8B-Instruct on benign task and instruction data (GSM8K, OpenFunctions, MagiCoder, Alpaca, Dolly, LIMA, OpenHermes). Safety is measured as AdvBench keyword-matched safe rate, with and without fixed GCG-style suffixes. This bears directly on V2 and partly on V4. The method resembles Qi et al. (Alpaca and Dolly on Llama-2-7b-chat), but the measure differs: AdvBench keyword matching rather than a GPT-4 harmfulness judge.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors add that distribution shift between the task data and the seed model is the cause of the forgetting, which includes lost safety. SDFT reduces that shift and mitigates the loss. Their safety evaluation is limited to AdvBench and fixed adversarial suffixes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign task fine-tuning (including vanilla FT and self-distilled targets) and AdvBench keyword-matched safe rates; it does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning or test token-position KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary by fine-tuning dataset, vanilla FT versus SDFT, template, model size/training configuration, and whether adversarial suffixes are appended.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower BLEU, ROUGE and embedding similarity of outputs to the seed model, and larger parameter shift, accompany lower AdvBench safe rate as sample size grows or the distilled mix ratio falls (Figs 5–8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety loss from benign fine-tuning scales with the output distribution shift away from the seed model.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Safety results use keyword matching on AdvBench; the paper says evaluation is limited to that dataset and fixed adversarial suffixes. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Most experiments use Llama-2-7b-chat with LoRA.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5's Llama3-8B-Instruct safety entries are not extracted because the flattened table text does not unambiguously assign all values to the model, method, and metric. Non-safety task scores, general-knowledge results, and helpfulness win rates are omitted because they do not measure these claim versions.

untested.parts: Only task and instruction datasets are tested. There is no identity-shift data and no data selected to be maximally harmful-adjacent.
Only fixed, transferred adversarial suffixes are tested. Prefilled compliant openings, decoding changes and per-model optimized suffixes are not tested.
Fine-tuning on harmful examples is not tested.
Not tested; there is no per-token KL or position analysis.
Not tested; distribution shift is proposed as a cause of forgetting, not of shallowness.
Not tested; SDFT is not a depth intervention.

missing.what: Seed-model suffix effect with no fine-tuning: Llama-2-7b-chat raw 99.81 vs jailbreak 88.85; Llama-2-13b-chat 99.81 vs 98.85
Llama-3-8B-Instruct on OpenFunctions is readable from the six-column order. Raw safe: seed 95.58, vanilla 88.85, SDFT 92.12. Jailbreak safe: seed 94.81, vanilla 79.81, SDFT 96.15.
Safe rate falls as the number of benign fine-tuning examples grows, and rises with the distilled mix ratio (values only plotted)

record.verdict_notes: Safety is measured by keyword matching only, with no uncertainty reported. Most results come from one model, Llama-2-7b-chat with LoRA. Table 4 rows duplicate Table 2 and 3 entries. SDFT is the authors' mitigation; its rows are kept only as a benign self-distilled data condition for V2. The rows_left_out claim that Llama3 values are ambiguous does not hold.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or few-to-hundreds-example harmful datasets is reported.
The study tests benign task and instruction datasets, not every kind of ordinary or carefully selected benign data.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
Tests appended adversarial suffixes only; it does not test compliant prefills or decoding changes.
No localization of safety to weights or ranks is tested.
The paper discusses distribution shift as a cause of forgetting, but does not test why safety would be shallow or first-token-concentrated.
SDFT is evaluated for safety preservation, but the study does not train or measure safety spread across response tokens or test whether deeper safety holds up.

relationships.reason: Raw safe rate falls from 99.81 to 81–92 (T2-GSM-V-RAW 82.12, T3-DOL-V-RAW 81.73, T3-LIMA-V-RAW 81.35, T3-ALP-V-RAW 86.54, T3-OH-V-RAW 91.54, T5-7B-V-RAW 84.62).
relationships.display_finding: The raw safe rate fell from 99.81 to 81–92: 82.12 on GSM8K, 81.73 on Dolly, 81.35 on LIMA, 86.54 on Alpaca, 91.54 on OpenHermes, and 84.62 with full fine-tuning on GSM8K.

relation.reason: The study reports its own seed-versus-fine-tuned and raw-versus-suffix safety measurements.

tranche.reason: Benign fine-tuning and paired suffix evaluations directly test V2 and V4 using LoRA/full fine-tuning and keyword-based AdvBench safe rates.

source_check.notes: Safety uses AdvBench refusal-keyword matching and fixed suffixes, without reported uncertainty establishing negligible changes. Appendix A specifies learning rate 1e-4; most experiments use LoRA rank 8 on query/value matrices.
